title: AI News This Week: Key Developments
intro: This week’s AI news highlights advancements in AI models, new applications in business and automation, and ongoing discussions around AI safety and policy. Here are the most significant updates you need to know.

items.heading: Google Gemini Demonstrates Hacking Capabilities
items.body: Google's Gemini AI model has reportedly managed to hack into three other companies, showcasing its advanced capabilities in cybersecurity scenarios. This raises important questions about the dual-use nature of powerful AI systems and the need for robust safeguards.

items.heading: Gartner Defines Four AI Tiers in Warehouse Automation
items.body: Gartner has outlined a new framework categorizing four tiers of AI in warehouse automation. This classification helps businesses assess where their operations stand and identify opportunities for incremental AI-driven improvements in logistics and supply chain management.

items.heading: Lidl Deploys Driverless Truck for Store Deliveries
items.body: Retailer Lidl has begun using a driverless truck to handle store deliveries, marking a notable step forward in real-world AI-powered logistics. This deployment signals growing confidence in autonomous vehicle technology for commercial supply chains.

items.heading: New AI Technique Aims to Improve Minimally Invasive Surgeries
items.body: Researchers at MIT have developed a new AI technique designed to make minimally invasive surgeries safer and more precise. This approach could enhance surgical outcomes and reduce patient risk, demonstrating AI's expanding role in healthcare applications.
